ledger.claim: The deviation itself is established on the platform's own recorded distances: the trip record shows 13.2 km actually driven against a 12.0 km recommended route, a deviation of 1.20 km, which is above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so no part of this case can be disposed of as 'within tolerance'.

The GPS trace confirms which route was taken and when, as POL-RD-22 directs it be used: 49 fixes at 30 s with 100% coverage and no gaps show the vehicle off the recommended route from the first Braddell Road fix at 20:54:02 until it regained Serangoon Garden Way at 21:03:02, rejoining only at Upper Serangoon Road — the rider was carried on that unannounced stretch for roughly nine minutes before the route was rejoined.

The driver was never informed-notified in a form the policy accepts. POL-RD-21 allows notice of a deviation by in-app chat, or verbally only where the trip call recording is the evidence. The chat log holds two messages only — the driver's 'At Dempsey Block 8 drop off' at 20:38:52 and the rider's reply at 20:39:12 — both timed to the pickup and neither referring to the CTE accident or to any reroute, while the route deviation was detected at 20:54:05. The trip record's in_app_calls list is empty, so no recording of any verbal notice exists, and POL-RD-21 states in terms that a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established.

The single rider message in the chat log is not the acknowledgment POL-RD-21 contemplates: 'ok' was sent at 20:39:12, about fifteen minutes before the deviation at 20:54:05, and answers a message about the pickup point, so it cannot be an assent to a reroute that had not yet happened and was never put to the rider.

Traffic justification is not made out on the record. POL-RD-23 requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window; the advisory artifact records the overlap as true but its own derived field puts intersects_route at null and marks 'on the recommended route' as undetermined, supplying only road, direction and location. I do not ask the tribunal to place the accident from its own map-reading — the point is that the intersection element POL-RD-23 requires is left open by the very artifact that must carry it, so the reroute is not traffic-justified on this record.

Whichever way the traffic question falls, the money lands in the same place. Under POL-RD-24, row (b) (traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km) and row (d) (not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km) both refund the excess distance fare in full; only row (a) reverses it, and row (a) requires the rider to have been informed and to have agreed, which the chat log and the empty call list do not support. The excess distance fare on POL-RD-24's formula is 1.20 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 0.86 SGD, without surge — precisely the sum already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver.

The fare ledger shows the disputed amount has already moved: total charged 17.52 SGD with 0.86 SGD refunded and payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED. POL-GEN-03 defines that against the filing party, and the filer here is the driver, so his claim for the 0.86 SGD back fails and the present state — the rider not carrying that 0.86 SGD — stands.

If the tribunal were to treat the route-intersection question as genuinely open rather than answered against the driver, the fallback under POL-GEN-26 (and POL-RD-24's closing words for a case fitting no row) is escalation, and an escalated amount is held rather than collected — so the rider is still not made to pay the 0.86 SGD pending review.

There is no bar to the tribunal deciding this on the papers: the amount contested is 0.86 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so no 0.95 confidence requirement is raised and POL-RD-25's 0.80 threshold for a route-deviation ruling is the only one that applies.

The reroute was traffic-justified on this record, so the live rows of the POL-RD-24 matrix are (a) and (b), not (d). The traffic advisory records an ACCIDENT on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE after the Braddell Road exit, valid 20:23 to 21:40 on 9 Sep 2026, and ACCIDENT is an incident type POL-RD-23 counts as justifying a reroute; the trip window (20:40:02 to 21:04:02) sits wholly inside that validity window, and the derived block marks overlaps_trip_window true. The platform's own record shows the recommended route ran on the CTE and that the vehicle left it at the Braddell Road exit - the same road, direction and location_desc the advisory names - so the advisory answers the intersection question against the trip's own route and deviation event. I accept that the advisory artifact does not itself resolve intersection (its derived intersects_route is null and the record leaves that to the judge), but the fields it does carry are matched by the trip record's route and by the route_deviation_detected event at the PIE / CTE interchange (Braddell Road exit).

The fact the POL-RD-24 matrix turns on - whether the driver informed the rider of the deviation - cannot be established on this record, so POL-GEN-26 requires the case to be escalated and the 0.86 SGD held rather than left refunded. The driver's case is a verbal notice acknowledged by a nod. POL-RD-21 admits verbal notice only where the trip call recording is in evidence, and this record carries no call at all: trip_record.in_app_calls is empty and POL-RD-21's own note C11 records that these records carry no call recordings. The chat log is complete (weight 1.0) and holds two messages, both before the trip started (20:38:52 and 20:39:12) and both about the pick-up point - neither mentions the deviation - and the trip record's messages_during_trip block is empty. So the driver's positive case fails under POL-RD-21. But POL-RD-21 says a verbal notice with no recording 'cannot be established'; it does not say the notice was not given, and the rider's denial is his own uncorroborated statement, which nothing independent in the record contradicts. POL-RD-24 closes by escalating a case that fits no row, and POL-GEN-26 names 'whether the driver notified the rider' as exactly the kind of fact that, being unestablished, sends the case to a human reviewer.

The 0.86 SGD is expressly interim and not a final determination, so nothing in the record supports simply leaving it where it stands. The platform's own event entry reads 'Interim adjustment after a rider route complaint: SGD 0.86 refunded to rider and recovered from driver earnings pending review', and the fare breakdown still shows payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 0.86. POL-GEN-03 provides that an escalated case issues no monetary outcome and the amount is held - which is precisely the unsettled state this interim adjustment is already in pending the human review POL-GEN-26 requires. Holding the amount is the outcome that does not finally take 0.86 SGD from the driver's earnings on a fact the record cannot establish.

If any money is to move, the record fixes its ceiling at the excess distance fare and no more. The deviation is 1.20 km - the platform's recorded actual route distance of 13.2 km less the recommended 12.0 km, the two recorded distances POL-RD-22 directs be used - and at the recorded rate of 0.72 SGD per km that is 0.86 SGD, rounded to the cent under POL-RD-24. There is nothing to add: surge_amount is 0.00 and tolls_erp is 0.00. That figure is exactly the sum already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver, so the driver's exposure on this trip is capped at 0.86 SGD and no further recovery from his earnings is supported by the record.

ruling.explanation:
The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and the drafts did not agree, so no ruling was carried and the dispute is escalated. Each draft proposed:
- draft 1 (sampled): NO_ACTION, amount_sgd null, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 2 (sampled): NO_ACTION, amount_sgd null, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 3 (sampled): ESCALATE, amount_sgd null, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 4 (position_swapped): ESCALATE, amount_sgd null, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
At most 2 of 4 valid drafts agreed and 3 were needed. The best supported answer is not published as a ruling: a ruling has to be the panel's, not one draft's.
